problem: The figure labels the cable block as 'up to 700 Ω', but 700 Ω is the maximum total loop resistance and it includes the 250 Ω sense resistor that appears as the next block. As drawn, a student reads that the cable alone may be 700 Ω, which contradicts the worked example and the exam trap saying R_loop,max counts cable both ways plus the sense resistor. The aria text ('up to 700 ohms total') also disagrees with the node note.
fix: Change the cable node note to 'up to 450 Ω' (700 Ω total minus the 250 Ω sense resistor), or relabel the node note as 'loop ≤ 700 Ω total' and keep the aria text consistent with it.

problem: 'Do not treat 4 mA as a measurement offset in the wire; the subtraction happens in software at the receiver' reads as if 4 mA is not an offset at all, while the section just defined live zero as exactly that. A student can carry away the wrong idea.
fix: Say it plainly: '4 mA is a real offset (the live zero). It is removed at the receiver when the voltage is scaled to engineering units, not by changing anything in the loop.'

problem: 'Burden voltage' is listed in the industry searches but is never defined anywhere in the chapter, so a reader meeting the term cold has nothing to attach it to.
fix: Add a short gloss: 'burden voltage — the voltage dropped across the sense resistor by the loop current, the load the transmitter must drive'.
